meta.title: Plugin System — KB Labs
meta.description: Install one package — get CLI commands, REST routes, and a Studio page automatically. Open SDK for your own plugins.

plugins.sdkLead2: ctx.ui.success() works the same from CLI or a Workflow step.
plugins.ctaDescription: Install KB Labs, run scaffold, add your logic. CLI, REST API, and Studio are ready automatically.
plugins.surfaceLead2: No router config, no command registration, no Studio config. Install the package — everything works.
plugins.sdkLead1: A plugin talks to abstractions — ctx.ui, useLLM(). Which provider is behind them, how requests are routed, where logs go — that's the platform's job.
plugins.lifecycleLead1: After install the platform records the package in .kb/marketplace.lock with a SHA-256 checksum. On every start, discovery verifies integrity and loads the manifest.
plugins.lifecycleLead2: The manifest extracts entity kinds — seven types: CLI commands, REST routes, Studio pages, workflow handlers, webhook handlers, WebSocket channels, cron schedules. One plugin can register any combination.
plugins.surfaceLead3: Plugins are isolated: each gets only the platform resources it declared. Full OS isolation available in container/remote execution mode.
plugins.lifecycleLead3: On command invocation the engine picks an execution backend. In-process is the default — minimal overhead. Subprocess and worker-pool add process isolation. Remote gives full OS isolation on a separate machine.
plugins.surfaceLead1: A plugin declares CLI commands, REST routes, and a Studio page in one file — manifest.ts. On install, the engine registers everything automatically.
plugins.permLead1: Every plugin declares in its manifest what it needs: read git, call LLM, write to fs. You see this before running install.
plugins.permLead2: This isn't a hard guarantee — with in-process execution the platform enforces declared permissions, but full OS isolation requires container or remote mode.
plugins.permLead3: Like mobile app permissions: you know what the plugin wants and make an informed decision.
plugins.heroDescription: Install one package — the engine registers CLI commands, REST routes, and a Studio page. No manual config. Permissions declared in the manifest — visible before install.

ecoSteps.title: Scaffold
ecoSteps.desc: Run kb scaffold run plugin my-plugin --yes. Manifest, handlers, and tsconfig in place.

ecoSteps.title: Implement
ecoSteps.desc: Write typed handlers. Import from @kb-labs/sdk only — no internal deps.

ecoSteps.title: Register
ecoSteps.desc: Install locally or publish to the marketplace. kb marketplace plugins list shows it immediately.
